input: strs is a nonempty list of N lowercase ASCII strings, where 1 <= N <= 100 and all strings have the same length M with 0 <= M <= 100. Empty strings are an explicit extension. Integer inputs are plain int values excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists and strings are ordinary str values, without subclasses or overloaded behavior. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The minimum number of column positions that must be deleted from every row so the resulting row list is lexicographically nondecreasing. This does not require characters within each row to be sorted, and no columns are actually removed.
mutation_aliasing: All input strings, the outer container and row order remain unchanged. A private Boolean flag for each adjacent row pair records whether retained earlier columns already establish a strict increase. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: All indices, lengths and the deletion count are in [-1,100] or [0,100] as applicable. ASCII character comparison agrees across languages. The count is exact; no string-to-number coercion occurs.
complexity: O(N*M+N+1) time and O(N+1) auxiliary space. A proposed column is first rejected if it reverses any unresolved adjacent pair; only accepted columns may mark pairs resolved. Each column scans adjacent pairs at most twice.
